purpose: Two questions, kept separate. (1) Does the harness help, holding the model constant - the original H0/H1/H2 variants. (2) Does the harness let a weak local model reach the operator's own play - the thesis arms below.

variants.description: Resolve zero/one eligible action without a model request.
Send only an allowlisted semantic snapshot and existing ActionChoice candidates to the local endpoint.
A controlled context-size ablation using the same provider, model, cases, and oracle; no new authority or action surface.

thesis.statement: Capability equals model times scaffold. Inside a bounded domain the scaffold substitutes for model capacity.
thesis.falsifiable_form: With one ~20B CPU model, the harness lifts operation from not-viable to within X percent of the operator's own play, while the model is consulted fewer than N times per 100 ticks.

arms.description: The operator playing by hand. This is the correct ceiling because the product premise is to act only through the visible surface a human player has.
The shipped configuration: local ~20B CPU model inside the full harness, measured against the ceiling on the same metrics.

deliberately_excluded.reason: The result is known in advance - an unscaffolded weak model cannot operate the client at all - so measuring it costs time and adds no information. Excluded by operator decision on 2026-09-19.
A frontier model would need either weights this CPU cannot host or a cloud call, and cloud_fallback is false. The operator's own play is the ceiling that matters and it needs neither.
